heroHeadline: US Strikes Iran Again After Hormuz Clash; Iran Missiles UAE; MOU Response Due — Day 70
heroSubtitle: Day 69 (May 7): The nominal ceasefire fractured further as Iran fired missiles, drones, and fast boats at three US Navy destroyers in the Strait of Hormuz, triggering US self-defense strikes on Iranian military facilities at Bandar Abbas and Qeshm Island — the first US strikes on Iranian territory since Rubio declared Operation Epic Fury 'effectively over' on May 5. The US Navy also disabled the rudder of an Iranian-flagged tanker in the Gulf of Oman for alleged blockade breach; Iran separately seized an oil tanker. Israel struck Beirut for the first time since the April 17 Lebanon ceasefire, while Hezbollah reported 17 targeted strikes on IDF forces. Diplomatically, Iran's FM Araghchi confirmed Tehran was 'finalising its views' on the US MOU framework — a one-page proposal calling for a 12–15 year enrichment moratorium, gradual sanctions relief, and Hormuz reopening within 30 days. Trump said deal was 'very possible' after 'very good talks' while simultaneously threatening Iran would be bombed 'a lot harder and more violently.' Day 70 (May 8): Iran launched 2 ballistic missiles and 3 drones at the UAE — all 5 intercepted by UAE defenses; 3 wounded. US and Iran exchanged fire overnight in Hormuz in a new self-defense exchange. Iran accused the US of ceasefire violations; Trump insisted the ceasefire was 'still in effect.' Rubio expected Iran's formal MOU response by end of May 8. Kalshi prediction markets showed rising odds of a US-Iran deal by 2027. Approximately 1,600 ships remain stranded with 23,000 sailors from 87 countries trapped in the Persian Gulf on Day 70. NBC News: the strait 'will take a long time to reboot' even after any deal.
